subject: Echelon Systems — Identity & Access Controls Questionnaire + Clarifications

Subject: Echelon IAM questionnaire submission (attached)

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for taking the time to respond to our security and identity questionnaire. Attached is our baseline IAM questionnaire for vendors — the team would like your completed responses by EOD next Wednesday (2025-09-10) so we can move to the procurement review.

Key areas of interest for us: SAML + OIDC support (IdP-initiated and SP-initiated), SCIM provisioning (user/entitlement sync, delta vs full), RBAC and delegated admin, admin session logging and tamper-evidence, certificate rotation processes, and tenant-level isolation for multi-tenant deployments.

I'll leave the primary questions in the sheet but call out one immediate ask: can Redwood support SCIM delta sync with filtering (to only provision users in a specific group) and return 2xx/4xx for individual operations so we can track per-user failures?

Attached: Echelon_IAM_Questionnaire_v1.xlsx (xlsx, 1 worksheet; 32 questions)

If you want to discuss live, we can schedule a short technical call later this week. Prefer weekdays 1:00–4:00 PM ET.

Best,
Samantha Cole

Echelon Systems

Hi Samantha — thanks for sending this over.

Acknowledged — we’ll scope the questionnaire and aim to have a first-pass response back by 2025-09-08, with a final reviewed package by 2025-09-10.

Quick responses to your immediate asks:
- SCIM: Redwood supports SCIM 2.0; we support delta sync semantics via change tokens and filtering by group attribute. Per-user operation results are returned with standard HTTP 2xx/4xx codes so your provisioning orchestration can act on partial failures.
- SSO: We support both SAML 2.0 (SP & IdP-initiated) and OIDC (authorization_code + PKCE for SP flows, and IdP-initiated OIDC with appropriate redirect URI configuration).

Kimberly (cc) will lead the questionnaire response and collect architecture artifacts. Ben — can you add the SCIM rate-limiting and certificate rotation notes to the draft?

We’re available for a technical call Thursday 2025-09-04 at 2:00 PM ET — does that work for Samantha?

Thanks,

Subject: Draft: Redwood responses to Echelon IAM questionnaire (attached)

Hi Samantha,

Attached is our draft response pack. It includes a completed questionnaire, a short SCIM architecture diagram, and a one-page summary of our SAML/OIDC support and admin controls.

Highlights (summary):
- SAML/OIDC: Support for IdP-initiated and SP-initiated SAML flows; OIDC auth_code + PKCE for browser/native flows; support for OIDC token introspection for long-lived API sessions. We support NameID formats (email, persistent, transient) and signed assertions with SHA-256. Certificate rotation: rolling key IDs with overlap period and automated JWK endpoint.
- SCIM provisioning: SCIM 2.0 endpoints; we expose filtering (eq, co, sw) on /Users and /Groups; delta sync via changeToken and /Bulk for batched ops. Per-resource result codes are provided; failed items are returned with detailed errorType and diagnostics in the response body.
- RBAC & admin controls: Built-in role hierarchy (Org Admin, Security Admin, Support Admin, App Admin) plus custom roles. Delegated admin supported via tenant-scoped admin roles; audit trail captures admin elevation events and approval workflow via the Console APIs.
- Session & audit: Immutable audit logs with append-only storage and HMAC-signed daily digests for tamper detection. Admin session controls include IP allowlisting, session idle timeouts, and enforced MFA for privilege escalation.

Attachments: Redwood_IAM_Response_v1.docx (docx), scim-arch-diagram.png (png)

Open questions we marked for Echelon:
1) Do you require SCIM Push (webhook-style) for immediate deprovision events, or is periodic pull-based delta sufficient?
2) For OIDC, do you need userinfo claims beyond email/name (we can pass custom claims via configured attribute release policies)?

We’ll join the call on Thursday 2025-09-04 at 2:00 PM ET — link below.

Zoom: https://redwood.zoom.us/j/9876543210

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Samantha Cole <samantha.cole@echelon-sys.com>

Date: Wed, 3 Sep 2025 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft: Redwood responses to Echelon IAM questionnaire (attached)

Thanks Kimberly — the draft looks thorough. A few clarification items from our engineering team before the call:

1) SCIM filtering: when you say "filtering by group attribute," can you confirm the exact query syntax you support (e.g., /Users?filter=groups.displayName eq "Redwood-Prod") and whether nested group-membership queries are supported?

2) Delta semantics: what is the retention window for changeToken history? We ask because we do weekly syncs and need at least a 7-day retention for missed tokens.

3) SCIM rate limits: what are the per-tenant RPS and burst limits, and do you offer quota exceptions for provisioning-heavy customers during cutovers?

4) Admin audit: Can you provide an example of the admin-elevation audit entry schema (timestamp, actor, target, reason, approval_id)? We want to ingest these into our SIEM.

5) OIDC claims: we require an email_verified claim and a custom claim for department and role. Is Redwood able to map LDAP/AD attributes into claims and sign them in the ID token?

6) Multi-tenant isolation: if we opt for dedicated pools (Redwood Dedicated), do admin roles remain tenant-scoped or are there cross-tenant admin operations possible by Redwood staff? We need contractual guarantees.

If you can drop short answers to these six items into the thread ahead of the call, that will speed the technical review.

Best,
Samantha

Hi Samantha — quick answers ahead of the call below. We’ll bring more detail on Thursday.

1) SCIM filtering: we support RFC7644 filters on /Users and /Groups; example: /Users?filter=groups.displayName eq "Redwood-Prod". Nested membership queries are supported when groups contain references to member resources; we return group membership arrays on /Users so you can evaluate membership client-side if needed.

2) Delta semantics: changeToken retention is configurable per-tenant; default retention is 14 days. During onboarding cutovers we can extend retention to 30 days for a short window.

3) SCIM rate limits: default is 10 RPS with a 100-request burst per tenant for SCIM endpoints; Dedicated customers can negotiate uplift or temporary exceptions during migrations. All rate limits are published per-tenant in the Console and surfaced via /limits API.

4) Admin audit schema (example):
- timestamp: 2025-09-03T14:55:12Z
- actor: kimberly.park@redwood.ai
- actor_display: "Kimberly Park"
- action: "grant_role"
- target: tenant:ech-12345:user:svc-account-01
- role: "Support Admin"
- reason: "on-call escalation"
- approval_id: "appr-20250903-77a"
We can publish the schema as JSON lines or as a syslog mapping for your SIEM.

5) OIDC claims: yes — we can map LDAP/AD attributes to ID token claims. email_verified is supported; custom claims (department, role) can be configured per-tenant and included in the ID token or userinfo endpoint. Claims are signed in the ID token; we support RSA and EC signing algorithms.

6) Multi-tenant isolation: for Redwood Dedicated, tenant admin roles remain tenant-scoped. Redwood operator access is restricted by IAM roles and just-in-time privileged access with approval; contractual language for no cross-tenant admin operations can be included in a Dedicated SOW.

Attachments: I attached a one-page JSON schema example for the audit event and a short note on rate limiting to the shared Drive folder.

See you on Thursday; Vivek will host the Zoom.

Best,
Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
